This is the ONLY tool you need for candidates.\n\nHOW RESULTS WORK\n- Returns candidates most experienced first, `limit` per page (default 20, max 100), starting at `offset` (default 0). Prefer narrowing with filters over paging deep; use `offset` to fetch the next page of an already-narrow search.\n- `total` is how many candidates match in all (often far more than one page); `count` is how many are in this response (<= `limit`).\n- Every returned candidate ALWAYS includes their full profile — hard skills (with years), education, work experience, languages, and contact/social links (phone, email, LinkedIn, GitHub, Telegram, portfolio). You never need a second call to read a profile; to answer 'what does X know / where did X work / how to reach X', just search for X.\n- Every returned candidate also carries a `documents` list (resume, photo, cover letter, ...). Each document has metadata — `atm_id`, `type`, `filename`, `mimetype`, `size_bytes`, `zipped`, `hash`, `source`, `uploaded` — and TWO ways to get the ORIGINAL file, pick either: `data_base64` (the file inline, base64 — render directly) OR `open_url` (fetch it from the server with the same Bearer token). Very large files omit `data_base64` (with a `data_note`) but `open_url` still works.\n- All filters are AND-combined (a candidate must satisfy every filter you set). Enum filters are case-insensitive and fuzzy: 'it' -> IT, 'senior' -> Senior.\n\nPICKING THE RIGHT FILTER (important)\n- Concrete technologies, tools, or hard skills -> `skills` (e.g. Python, React, Figma, Excel), NOT `query`. `skills` requires ALL listed skills; aliases and typos are auto-resolved (js -> JavaScript, k8s -> Kubernetes).\n- Job title -> `position`; current job title only -> `current_position`; seniority -> `role_level`; business sector -> `industry`.\n- Vague or descriptive wording that is not a concrete field -> `query` (free text over name/position/workplace/description). It matches per word (order-independent), ignores words absent from the data, and understands role synonyms (programmer/coder/SWE -> developer/engineer).
